messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Discharge Summary:

Patient: 25-year-old female
Admission date: [DATE]
Discharge date: [DATE]
Length of stay: [NUMBER] days
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the emergency department with complaints of acute onset of epigastric pain and nausea with bilious emesis. Initial workup did not demonstrate evidence of biliary or gallbladder pathology. However, her symptoms progressed and she was re-evaluated with a computed tomography that demonstrated a soft tissue mass located posterior to the gallbladder. Further evaluation with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography observed a complex cystic structure of indeterminate etiology at the porta hepatis.

The patient underwent surgery, during which a hemorrhagic pedunculated mass attached to the infundibulum of the gallbladder was identified and resected. A cholecystectomy was also performed due to inflammation from the hemorrhagic mass. Gross pathology and histology revealed a hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue, and localized cholecystitis in the area adjacent to the mass was also observed.

The patient's postoperative course was uneventful and her symptoms resolved immediately. She was discharged home on the first postoperative day and was asymptomatic when seen in follow-up.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to remove the hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue and cholecystitis. She was discharged with instructions to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient was asymptomatic and in stable condition at the time of discharge.

Discharge Medications: N/A

Follow-up:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is a hemorrhagic pedunculated mass of benign ectopic liver tissue (accessory liver) attached to the gallbladder; the localized cholecystitis was secondary to it. Ectopic liver tissue is a congenital malformation, which falls in chapter Q. It is classified under congenital malformations of the gallbladder, bile ducts and liver, category Q44.

CODE: Q44
